broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Establishes the theoretical framework for why gut microbiome matters in lung cancer, relevant to any discussion of extraintestinal effects of gut microbes.
broader_review_uses.material: Description of the bidirectional network connecting intestinal microbiota with pulmonary health via immune, neural, and metabolic pathways.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Background context on the gut-lung axis concept

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Provides practical examples of how microbiome modulation is being explored clinically, useful for discussing future directions or intervention strategies.
broader_review_uses.material: Discussion of probiotics, prebiotics, FMT, and dietary interventions as adjuncts to immunotherapy.

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Allows for comparison of microbiome-Ici interactions across different solid tumors, though the primary focus remains lung cancer.
broader_review_uses.material: Brief mentions of melanoma, renal, and bladder carcinomas regarding antibiotic impact on ICIs.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Focuses primarily on lung cancer; while it mentions other cancers briefly, the detailed evidence is lung-specific. Causal inference is limited to observational associations and preclinical models.
facet_contributions.contribution: Details the correlation between specific gut microbiota compositions (e.g., A. muciniphila, SCFA-producing bacteria) and improved clinical outcomes in solid tumors treated with ICIs. It also notes that antibiotic use negatively impacts ICI efficacy.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Can be used to support arguments about the positive or negative influence of specific microbial taxa on ICI efficacy in solid tumors. Provides examples of predictive biomarkers.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Mechanisms are often derived from mouse models or inferred from human correlative data. The review acknowledges complexity and multiple interacting pathways rather than a single linear mechanism.
facet_contributions.contribution: Elaborates on mechanisms including: 1) Metabolite-mediated regulation (SCFAs, acetate, butyrate influencing immune cell function); 2) Immune cell priming and trafficking (dendritic cells, T-cell activation, CD8+ T cell infiltration); 3) Direct translocation of bacteria to tumor sites; 4) Modulation of bile acid metabolism affecting Treg migration.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Provides specific mechanistic pathways to explain how gut microbes affect tumor immunity and drug response. Useful for detailing the biological basis of microbiome-immunotherapy interactions.

planning_summary: This review serves as a foundational resource for understanding the gut-lung axis in lung cancer, particularly its impact on immunotherapy efficacy. It provides detailed descriptions of microbial signatures associated with ICI response, mechanistic pathways involving metabolites and immune cells, and emerging therapeutic strategies. It is highly relevant for facets concerning how the microbiome modulates ICI efficacy and the underlying mechanisms.
scope_interpretation_cautions: The review is a narrative synthesis, not a systematic review or meta-analysis; therefore, it does not provide pooled effect sizes or rigorous statistical aggregation of all available evidence.
Many mechanistic claims are based on preclinical (mouse) models or correlative clinical studies; causal relationships in humans are not definitively proven within this text.
The term 'solid tumours' in the user's plan is broader than the paper's primary focus on lung cancer; users must extrapolate carefully when applying lung-specific findings to other solid tumors.
title: The gut microbiome in lung cancer: from pathogenesis to precision therapy
